newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha weaker on overseas crude plunge.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha weaker on overseas crude plunge.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices fell for the second successive business day in subdued afternoon trade on Monday, in reaction to a fall in crude oil prices on Friday's overseas markets, traders said.
Trading remained lacklustre with markets in China, Singapore and Taiwan closed for the Chinese New Year.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half April was notionally assessed at $233.00/236.00. On Friday, it was sold to a western trader at $238.50.
Second-half April was quoted at $230.00/232.50 on Monday, down from late Friday's $234.00/235.50.

In inter-month naphtha spreads, backwardation for near-term cargoes steepened, with bids for second-half March/second-half April heard at plus $8.50. Offer levels were unclear, but traders estimated them to be in "double digits."
The spread deepened as market participants were concerned about physical tightness for second-half March on the back of reasonable demand, traders said.
First-half April/first-half May was quoted at around plus $6.00/8.00, slightly wider than Friday's plus $6.00/7.50.
